title: Catenarity is detected on an affine open cover
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $S=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be a covering by affine open subschemes. If every ring $\mathcal O_S(U_i)$ is catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring], then for every affine open subscheme $V\subseteq S$ the ring $\mathcal O_S(V)$ is catenary.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $V\subseteq S$. By [lem-trf-affine-catenary-chain-criterion], applied to $T=V$, it suffices to bound finite strict-chain lengths and equate saturated-chain lengths in each interval $[Z,Z']_V$ of irreducible closed subsets. Fix such $Z\subseteq Z'$. Irreducibility includes nonemptiness [def-weil-irreducible-components], so choose $x\in Z$. Since the $U_i$ cover $S$, choose $i$ with $x\in U_i$.

Apply [lem-trf-overlapping-open-irreducible-intervals] in the underlying space of $S$ to $U=U_i$, $V$, and $Z\subseteq Z'$. Its hypothesis $Z\cap U_i\ne\varnothing$ holds by $x$. With $W=V\cap U_i$, it gives irreducible closed $C=\overline{Z\cap W}^{\,U_i}\subseteq C'=\overline{Z'\cap W}^{\,U_i}$ and inverse bijections between the entire intervals $[Z,Z']_V$ and $[C,C']_{U_i}$, preserving strict- and saturated-chain lengths. No affineness of $W$ is used.

The hypothesis makes $\mathcal O_S(U_i)$ catenary. Since $U_i$ is affine, [lem-trf-affine-catenary-chain-criterion] gives a finite bound on strict-chain lengths in $[C,C']_{U_i}$ and equality of its saturated-chain lengths. By [lem-trf-overlapping-open-irreducible-intervals], a chain in $[Z,Z']_V$ has the same length as its image, and saturated chains correspond in both directions. Thus the same bound and equality hold in $[Z,Z']_V$. A saturated chain exists as well: the nonempty set of attainable lengths is a bounded subset of $\mathbf N$, hence has a largest member, and a chain of that length admits no insertion.

The pair $Z\subseteq Z'$ was arbitrary, so [lem-trf-affine-catenary-chain-criterion] gives catenarity of $\mathcal O_S(V)$. The same criterion covers empty $V$: there are no irreducible closed pairs, and its coordinate ring is the zero ring with no primes. An empty indexing set can cover only the empty scheme, so this also covers the empty-cover case. Finally $V$ was arbitrary among affine opens, proving the statement.
